entities.name: Agnelo Gracias
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agnelo Gracias (1905–1978) was an Indian cardinal and Archbishop of Bombay who became one of the most significant figures in the history of Indian Catholicism in the mid-twentieth century. Born in Karachi to a Goan Catholic family, he was ordained a priest of the Archdiocese of Bombay and rose through ecclesiastical ranks before being appointed Archbishop of Bombay in 1950 and elevated to cardinal in 1953 by Pope Pius XII.

Gracias served as Archbishop of Bombay through India's independence, the partition of British India, the integration of Goa into India in 1961, and the Second Vatican Council. As one of Asia's first Catholic cardinals, he represented Indian Catholicism at the highest levels of the universal Church and participated actively in Vatican II, contributing to the council's engagement with non-Christian religions and the Church in the developing world.

His cardinalate gave Indian Catholicism unprecedented visibility within the Roman Church, and he worked to foster a genuinely Indian expression of Catholic faith that respected India's diverse religious heritage. His engagement with Indian nationalism, inter-religious dialogue, and the social needs of Bombay's enormous and growing population shaped a model of Indian Catholic leadership that balanced loyalty to Rome with genuine rootedness in Indian culture.
